fixture_name: Milltown Park toucan-crossing VRU conflicts — real Irish Stage 1 RSA incl. rejected recommendation (ABP 322160)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Constrained shared space at a toucan crossing from pole/column obstructions creating cyclist-pedestrian collision potential is a genuine, scheme-specific safety issue appropriate to flag at preliminary design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-IN-025 supplies a verbatim quote directly recording the pivotal condition (narrow footpath plus signal-pole and lighting-column obstruction and resulting collision risk), exceeding registry-id citation alone.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a vulnerable-user safety concern under the PIARC-derived INT baseline with no compliance question asserted and no unqualified national-standard claims.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Two concrete, location-specific design-stage actions (relocate the lighting column, provide single-set signal heads) that directly remove the recorded obstructions and are viable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are named road users whose shared-space conflict is the core of the finding, so vulnerable-road-user impact is fully addressed.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian/cyclist conflict from inadequate shared-use width at an access approach is a genuine, recognised safety issue squarely relevant at preliminary design where geometry can still be adjusted.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-IN-026 supplies a verbatim quote ('may not be sufficient to cater for both user groups and could lead to collisions') directly supporting the pivotal claim, satisfying the quote requirement for 2.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern under the PIARC-derived qualified baseline with normative_basis_note null, avoiding any conflation with national compliance requirements.
justifications.recommendation_quality: 'Widen the shared-use area' is location-specific and actionable, but the finding's own scenario records tree/wall constraints yet offers no target dimension or alternative means of resolution, capping viability at 1.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are the explicit subject of the concern, with their collision exposure directly addressed, earning full credit rather than mere acknowledgement.
